title: fix(deps): repair vulnerable packages and verify consumer compatibility
body:
## Summary

Repair the backend dependency graph without changing production code, schemas, contracts, feature flags or runtime permissions. Pin direct dependencies to their resolved versions, apply consumer-scoped security fixes, restore compatible instrumentation dependencies and add eight real-package compatibility tests.

**Draft only.** Commit `238f0f1f152ebbb1b4691f555e98c888473d8ee7` preserves exact frozen product tree `b2bb1666a91d60927d3ee1d6455ce687ce1c8739`, based on `c23b9d9f3fcc106b92c061ceb7d04d7ec53038d7`. Builder verdict is FINDINGS, not independent review or release approval.

## Linked plan / brief

- [Dependency repair brief](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/tgp-agent-context/blob/9a15a618113ff5969a59724ff1fcd5b7496013da/handoffs/op80-execution/cycle2-dependency-builder-brief.md)
- [Three-PR dependency and ownership plan](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/tgp-agent-context/blob/9a15a618113ff5969a59724ff1fcd5b7496013da/handoffs/op80-execution/NEXT_THREE_PR_CONCURRENCY.md)

## Scope and compatibility

Only `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `test/dependency-compatibility.spec.ts` change. All 55 direct versions are exact; only three direct resolved versions change: js-yaml 4.2.0 to 4.3.2, ws 8.20.1 to 8.21.0 and Danger 12.3.4 to 13.0.8. The lock delta includes 85 differing package nodes and is not represented as only three changed packages.

Prisma/client 6.19.3 and existing Nest versions remain unchanged. Deepmerge, Multer and Swagger YAML overrides are scoped to the actual consuming parent. Removing the global minimatch override restores each caller's supported major and real Babel instrumentation. No forced install, audit suppression, omitted dev dependencies, library fork or package-lock surgery.

## Test plan

- **Security:** Full npm audit improved from 26 findings to zero across all severities, including dev dependencies. Real old shell-quote and deepmerge negative checks remain preserved.
- **Real package behavior:** Eight assertion-bearing probes cover shell quoting, cyclic merging, native Prisma/c12 loading, Istanbul selection, Swagger/NYC YAML, Danger Git reads, Multer parsing and WebSocket frames. They reject spawn errors, signals, nonzero exits, unexpected stderr and missing completion markers.
- **Exact final full suite:** 531 suites, 7,857 tests and six snapshots passed on frozen tree b2bb; exit zero. Twelve inherited skipped suites, 159 skipped tests and five todos remain, not introduced or relabeled as passing.
- **Earlier compilation evidence:** Typecheck, build and focused Babel coverage passed before the final manifest-only override-scope correction. All installed executable/test/generated bytes and lockfile bytes were proven invariant through that correction; these earlier runs are not described as fresh final-tree executions.
- **Graph and SBOM:** Final sequential npm graph, CycloneDX SBOM and no-op resolution recurrence checks passed. The local SBOM has 1,117 components; an every-PR uploaded SBOM enforcer remains outstanding.
- **Failure provenance:** The first full run failed because its evidence guard rejected test-owned HTTP listeners. A separately controlled same-process loopback guard admitted only test-owned ephemeral HTTP ports; all 95 previously failed test identities were covered by the targeted correction and final full suite. This is cooperative test isolation, not an OS security sandbox.
- **Publication hooks:** Actual installed lefthook 2.1.9 pre-commit and commit-msg hooks passed on commit 238f0f1f: tsc, staged ESLint, staged Prettier, banned tokens and identity-message check. The optional quick-readiness script is absent, so its conditional no-op is N/A, not an executed readiness pass. Private hash-verified dependency and formatter copies were used with no install, network event or product-byte change; the producer's entire installed dependency content was reverified unchanged afterward.
- **Remote CI:** Completed on a verified identical-content synthetic merge; see the current verification update below. Independent review remains pending.

## Rollback plan

No production deployment or migration is authorized by this draft. If the dependency change later causes a regression, revert its single commit through the ordinary reviewed pipeline and restore the prior known deployment while investigating; reverting reintroduces the known package advisories and is containment, not a security fix. No database rollback, contract downgrade or flag change is involved.

## R138 Decision Gate

- **Musk five principles:** Question the need for unrelated major upgrades; delete the incompatible broad override, simplify to consumer-compatible fixes, accelerate independent preparation and automate checks only after preserving their assertions. The ordered process is described by [Inc.](https://www.inc.com/jeff-haden/elon-musks-algorithm-a-5-step-process-to-dramatically-improve-nearly-everything-is-both-simple-brilliant.html).
- **Hyperscaler practice:** Use isolated, immutable inputs and staged safety gates rather than equating build success with release approval, consistent with [AWS continuous-delivery guidance](https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/going-faster-with-continuous-delivery/).
- **GOOD without BAD:** Remove known vulnerable dependencies and unblock downstream diagnostics without production edits, shared writable tooling, concealed failures or premature deployment.
- **Root cause:** Repair the resolved dependency graph and caller API compatibility, not audit output or coverage-provider settings. The test network guard and report integrity are separately disclosed evidence concerns.

This decision authorizes draft publication, not merge or deployment. Blast radius is a three-path branch with an exact reconstructable tree; parent alone owns remote actions.

## Dependencies and remaining blockers

Diagnostics is a separate sequential PR based on this frozen dependency tree. Its combined preparation would be 490 workflow net lines, so it will not be folded into this PR. Database recovery, C1 durable intent and mobile/extension consumers remain farther down the dependency chain.

Live backend branch protection, an eligible independent GitHub reviewer, effective fail-closed SAST, exact-head CI and repository-wide enforcement gaps remain unresolved. The existing CodeQL workflow's `continue-on-error` and GHAS detection mean a nominal green check alone is insufficient. No permissions/settings have been changed and no inherited control is waived.

## Notes for auditor

Audit the exact published head and complete diff from c23, with all matrix inputs pinned independently of the moving documentation branch. Review override scope stability, caller-major preservation, spawn completion assertions, retained negative evidence and the distinction between local SBOM output and remote enforcement. A diagnostics candidate, builder self-check or predecessor CI result is not an audit of this PR.

## Current verification update

Remote CI completed with 531 suites, 7,857 tests and six snapshots passed; 12 inherited skipped suites, 159 skipped tests and five todos remain. Actual CodeQL analysis 1796271510 completed with 201 rules, zero results and no error. GitHub checked synthetic merge 0786a9f087d8dcec7dfb8d1271c78aeba5baabb3 with tree b2bb1666a91d60927d3ee1d6455ce687ce1c8739, exactly equal to this candidate, and parents c23b9d9/238f0f1. This is exact-content evidence, not product-commit checkout or deployment approval. The conditional deployment gate was skipped. Independent Astra/Fable audits are running on fixed inputs; inherited enforcement findings remain open.

## R100 Self-Check

The following complete 55+18 tables preserve the builder's historical closeout, not an independent audit. Current publication/remote evidence is stated above; unresolved controls remain unresolved. [Full archived evidence and provenance](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/tgp-agent-context/blob/9a15a618113ff5969a59724ff1fcd5b7496013da/handoffs/op80-execution/build-reports/backend-dependency/BUILD_REPORT.md) preserves the original links, findings and chronology; local evidence references are not claimed to be remotely accessible.
